references.finding: A large white desktop window with black titlebar overlaps monochrome corner photos on cobalt blue.
Blue masthead above a white directory window with a narrow monochrome horse plate.
Large right chapter numeral and left white chapter title above a shallow window.
Black label bands and white prose areas express the desktop motif; no placeholder six-item list retained.
Text moves between white-on-blue and black-on-white fields; a monochrome building anchors the opposite corner.
Chapter identity deliberately shares reference2 layout with different numeral and title.
A gray parent window contains an architectural plate and two white prose panes.
Closing title sits in a large window; source name, date, pinyin and logos are not content.

limitations: Photographs are restricted to clean reference pixels; window chrome is native decorative geometry, not working interface controls.

cover.designReason: A broad white native window carries the complete title and scope on cobalt desktop.

toc.designReason: White-on-blue directory title above a wide numbered window, echoing the reference without source branding.

chapter.designReason: Shared chapter window with full editable chapter numeral and title; no sample paragraph is introduced for an empty chapter body.

ending.designReason: A closing window uses centered typography and the original action sentence.

content.designReason: A white-on-blue masthead introduces one full-width document window; the source sections run successively as an article.

contentVariants.designReason: A white-on-blue masthead introduces one full-width document window; the source sections run successively as an article.
The title occupies the blue left sidebar and the full article reads vertically inside a tall right document window.
Four narrow open-file columns carry consecutive complete source clauses left to right; the headline closes below the whole four-column sequence.
A black headline bar divides two full-width source sections, with the upper section directly on blue and the lower inside a white document.
Two parallel files open with the complete source sections; a broad white title closes below both files.
A full-width opening section precedes a lower-left headline and a lower-right continuation window.
The main title forms the center column between two complete source sections, all inside one wide parent window.
The upper title and first section occupy a narrow-wide split; the second section expands across a full-width white reply window.
The left source section starts under the headline; the right section begins near the top in a separate tall window.
Both source sections run in one left document; a headline and monochrome facade occupy the right desktop area.
A title window occupies the upper-left corner while the first section sits to its right; the second section steps down to a wide lower-left file.
An upright desktop title faces three consecutive newspaper columns within one white document; the second source section continues into the last column instead of becoming a full-height right block.
A wide masthead and full-width first section lead to a narrower lower-left continuation, opposite an architectural plate.
The headline crosses the middle of the desktop between an upper-right source window and a lower-left source window.
The heading is carried inside the top of a wide window, with two side-by-side source sections below its internal dividing rule.
A continuous broad article occupies the upper white window; the title signs off across the lower blue field.
Two narrow source columns share a white left window, while a large upright title occupies the blue right edge.
A broad first section opens at the top, the second continues in a narrow middle-left window, and the centered title closes below both.
A compact top title is followed by two numbered horizontal prose rows in one window; actual section order supplies both ordinals.
The first section forms a tall left text margin; the title sits at upper-right and the second section returns across the lower-right window.
A white title and first section share a large upper window; the second section is an inset gray sheet breaking below its right edge.
A broad opening section fills the upper window; the lower continuation sits at left while the title appears in a separate lower-right white pane.
The first section reads under a numeral in the left window; the second begins one level lower in the right, under a title-bearing black bar.
The headline is centered at the top of the desktop; the first source section sits in a compact middle window and the second flows across the bottom blue band.
The source sections begin at opposite corners of the upper desktop; the headline is contained in a bottom-left window that completes a descending three-step reading path.

visualAcceptance.scope: Complete 30-page principal image/text and reading-path review including nonadjacent and cross-role comparisons. Exact unchanged PNG carryover is identified below.
limitations: Isolated actual HTTP export only; not deployment acceptance.
